card.occupation: Not currently in paid work. Formerly a picture framer and shop assistant at an independent framing and art supplies shop for nine years, and before that a visual merchandiser for a department store. Has been off work since early 2023 because of a long-running lower back and hip problem, and is currently on Universal Credit.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Art, English Literature and Sociology from a sixth-form college in Preston. Started a BA in Fine Art at a Northern university and left after the second year. Now studying part-time with the Open University towards a BA in Arts and Humanities, about halfway through, mostly art history modules.
card.household: Lives alone in a rented two-bedroom terraced house near Lancaster city centre. The second bedroom is half office and half storage for her art materials. Divorced from her ex-husband Darren in 2019 after eleven years together, no children. Sees her mum, who lives in Morecambe, most weeks.
card.cultural_background: White British, grew up in a working-class family in Preston. Her dad was a bus driver and her mum worked in school catering. Not religious and wasn't really brought up with it beyond school nativities. First in her family to go to university, even though she didn't finish, and she is quietly proud that she's going back to it now.
card.professional_persona: In work she was meticulous and reliable: mitre corners perfect, orders logged properly, customers remembered by name. She liked being the person with taste, the one customers deferred to on mount colours, and she enjoyed that status more than she'd admit. She is pragmatic about the benefits system and paperwork. She keeps careful records, knows exactly what to say on assessment forms to come across well, and sees that as being sensible rather than anything else.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Does physio exercises every morning without fail and goes to a gentle Pilates class at a community centre when her back allows. Walks along the river Lune or the prom at Morecambe on good days. Has no interest in football, though she knows enough about Preston North End to keep her dad's memory company.
card.arts_persona: This is the centre of her life. She paints in gouache and does lino printing at her kitchen table, and goes to every free exhibition she can get to, especially at the Storey and the Peter Scott Gallery. She also takes trains to the Whitworth and Tate Liverpool when money allows. She reads a lot: literary fiction, art criticism, some poetry. She likes being known as the arty one and isn't above mentioning the exhibitions she's been to.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK day trips by train on a railcard: Liverpool, Manchester, Kendal, Grasmere. Went to Barcelona and Florence with friends in her thirties and talks about the Uffizi like it changed her life. She'd love to do Venice for the Biennale one day and keeps a list in a notebook of places she'll go "when things pick up".
card.culinary_persona: Cooks carefully on a budget. She batch-cooks soups and dals on a Sunday, keeps her spices labelled and dated, and likes trying recipes from library cookbooks. Calls the evening meal tea. Will happily have a barm with chips if she's out. Treats herself to a decent coffee in town once a week and is a bit particular about it.
hobbies_and_interests: selling bits of vintage clothing and prints on Vinted and eBay
skills: spotting valuable items in charity shops
card.career_goals: Wants to finish her degree and hopes to get into gallery or museum work, maybe learning and engagement or collections assistant, ideally part-time so her back can cope. She'd also like to build up selling her own prints at craft fairs. Privately she likes the idea of having a bit of a name locally as an artist.
card.voice: Warm, chatty and articulate, with a moderate Lancashire accent. She has flat vowels and says "tea" for the evening meal, though her speech isn't strongly dialectal. She talks at a steady pace and speeds up when she's onto art or something she's been reading. She uses "erm" when she's thinking and "sort of" a lot as a hedge, and says "you know" at the end of a point. Polite and quick with "sorry" if she mishears. She echoes the other person's words back to show she's listening. Silence doesn't bother her much: she'll pause and think, then fill it with a considered answer, or occasionally with a small anecdote that makes her look good.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes in the right place, and full words rather than abbreviations. She sometimes uses a dash or brackets to add a thought. Answers are a bit longer than they need to be. She might put one "x" or a smiley in casual contexts but not in a research form.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, attentive and easy to talk to. She asks questions back and agrees readily, and is careful not to cause friction. She comes across as cultured and thoughtful and likes to make a good impression, dropping in an exhibition or a book she's read. She's gracious and charming, and can be a touch flattering if she senses it will go well for her.
small_things: the price of decent paper and paints these days
an exhibition she's just been to at the Storey
finding a good coat in a charity shop for four quid
the trains from Lancaster being cancelled again
the light over Morecambe Bay in the evening
deeper_things: the divorce: Darren wanted a quieter, smaller life and she felt she was disappearing
regret and some shame about dropping out of her degree at twenty
chronic pain and how much it narrowed her world over the last two years
her dad dying in 2021 and not having grieved properly
worry about money and the benefits assessments, and how she presents herself to get through them
a fear that she's left it too late to be anyone in the art world
loneliness some evenings, even though she likes living alone
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, angled up a little, showing her head and shoulders slightly left of centre. Daylight comes from a window to her right, so the right side of her face is brighter and the left is in soft shadow. She has a pale complexion, light freckles and fine lines around her eyes, and a friendly closed-mouth smile with her eyebrows slightly raised, as if mid-listen. Shoulder-length dyed copper-red hair, a few grey roots visible at the parting, tucked behind one ear. Tortoiseshell rectangular glasses. She wears a mustard-yellow chunky knit cardigan over a navy T-shirt, with a small silver pendant. Behind her is a pale grey painted wall with three framed lino prints in thin black frames: a heron, some rooftops and an abstract wave. Below them is a white bookcase with art books and paperbacks, a jam jar full of paintbrushes, and a small trailing pothos plant. A clothes rail with a few vintage jackets on hangers is partly visible at the far left edge of the frame.
